Where things stand
I reconstructed the full working tree from dump.txt and verified it: all 336 files match their recorded SHA-256 (the one apparent mismatch, export.sh, is an artifact of the script printing its own # FILE: header — stitched and verified separately at 674c5cc…).

The last run was fully green. Slice 36's predicted 1082 was not a prediction any more:

Test summary: total: 1082, failed: 0, succeeded: 1082, skipped: 0
§16.3 end to end: 16 of 16
all local CI gates passed  (8 of 8)
Smoke, compose-substitution preflight, quick tunnel, and the container stack all came up clean. So nothing is broken, and this session is about what the green run printed past.

Three findings, and I stopped before packaging
1. A high-severity advisory is riding in the tree, printed twice on every restore.

warning NU1903: Package 'SSH.NET' 2025.1.0 has a known high severity vulnerability
I pulled the advisory rather than guessing at it. CVE-2026-48798, CVSS 7.1, published 2026‑08‑12 — one day before your dump. ScpClient recursive download writes files using server-supplied names without checking containment, so a malicious SCP server can traverse out of the download directory. Vulnerable range <= 2025.1.0; first patched version 2026.0.0, released 2026‑08‑09, whose notes say "Breaking changes: None known".

Three facts that make the repair easy and the reasoning honest:

Testcontainers 4.13.0 pins SSH.NET at exactly 2025.1.0 (confirmed in their Directory.Packages.props at that tag), which is how it reaches both test projects.
ScpClient appears zero times in the whole testcontainers-dotnet repository, and this tree never mentions Renci, SshNet, ScpClient or SftpClient anywhere. The vulnerable call site is unreachable here — so the pin is about noise, not exposure, and the ledger row should say so.
2025.1.0 targets net462;netstandard2.0;net8.0;net9.0 — no net10.0. 2026.0.0 adds net10.0. So the pin also stops the test projects resolving a down-level asset.
CentralPackageTransitivePinningEnabled is already true, so this is one <PackageVersion> line — and NSubstitute in that same file is already a version pinned with nothing referencing it, so the pattern has precedent I can point at.

2. ci_local.sh names its one gap and it has two. The header states "The one gate this cannot reproduce is CI's boot-smoke job." But ci.yml also runs a vulnerable package audit (advisory) step, and no local gate corresponds to it. That is exactly why finding 1 was invisible: the eight-gate run a developer executes on purpose never asks the question. Adding the audit locally, non-blocking as in CI, makes that sentence true again rather than weakening it.

3. check_tree.sh gate 3 prints a claim one word stronger than its check — and I reproduced the eleven files independently. The gate checks for CR and for a final newline, then prints "all files end with exactly one LF." Nothing checks "exactly." Eleven authored files end with two:

.env.example                                    scripts/backup.sh
.github/workflows/ci.yml                        scripts/restore_drill.sh
…/Account/Pages/SignIn.razor                    …/Identity/AccountEndpoints.cs
…/Counter/CounterBoard.razor                    …/Identity/IdentityServiceCollectionExtensions.cs
…/Identity/ObligationsEnforcement.cs            …/Harness/CounterJourneys.cs
…/Identity/IdentityWiringTests.cs
I did not read that count out of BUILD_PROGRESS.md — each surfaced as a one-byte SHA delta during reconstruction, before I knew the item was carried. Zero CR, zero missing final newline. Gate 2 legitimately passes, since an empty line is not a whitespace-only line under ^[[:space:]]+$.

What I've confirmed about the environment before writing anything
I can actually run the shell gates. bash 5.2 and git are present; I initialised a scratch repo over the reconstructed tree and check_tree.sh runs green against it, reporting the same 336 authored files. So gate 3's new check gets executed and proven sensitive, not predicted.
No .NET SDK here, so any C# is unverified by compilation — the F-71 lesson. That shapes the next decision.
TestingSectionContractTests is the real constraint on documentation: any §16.4 paragraph citing one *Tests.cs in backticks and stating a number before "assertions" must match that file's [Fact]/[Theory] count, ten paragraphs must state one, and a paragraph naming two classes alongside any count is a hard failure.
One decision before I package
Findings 1 and 3 are shell and MSBuild only — I can execute both here. Finding 2's repair is also shell. The open question is whether to add a new C# contract test holding the audit command in ci.yml and ci_local.sh together. It is the project's established pattern for one-fact-in-two-files (F-48, F-50, F-56, F-65, F-73) and without it the two can be silently unpaired again — but it is a new C# file I cannot compile, which is exactly how Slice 35 lost a whole project's assertions.

My inclination is to include it, kept to two facts using only the proven FindRepositoryRoot idiom, with the honest note in BUILD_PROGRESS.md that nothing compiled it. Say the word and I'll build the archive — full files, repo-relative, one extraction at the root, a git add line for anything new, an explicit "Files to DELETE" section, and spec bumped to v1.22 with ledger rows and changelog moving together. Or tell me to drop the C# and ship a slice that is entirely verified here, and the parity gate becomes a named open item instead.
